subject: Draft case study: TideWave Analytics — quote verification and publish timeline
messages:
From: Sophie Li <sophie.li@tidewave.io>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@tidewave.io>
Date: 2026-08-09T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Draft case study + quote — can you review

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for the interview last week. We've put together a first-pass draft of the case study and included the customer-facing quote we discussed. Please find the draft attached (TideWave_CaseStudy_Draft_v1.docx). We want to make sure the technical details and the quote are accurate before we publish the customer story on Aug 20.

Quick asks: 1) Can you confirm the final quote language below ("Redwood reduced inference costs by ~45% with our batching and quantization mix")? 2) Any legal or compliance flags we should be aware of? 3) If everything looks okay, can we get final approval and a headshot/logo by EOD next Thursday (8/19)?

Happy to hop on a short call if useful.

Best,
Sophie Li
Head of Marketing, TideWave Analytics
Sophie Li | TideWave Analytics
Attachments: TideWave_CaseStudy_Draft_v1.docx (docx, 420 KB)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sophie Li <sophie.li@tidewave.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-10T10:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft case study + quote — can you review

Thanks, Sophie — nice first pass. A few quick notes from product/marketing perspective:

- Quote accuracy: the number feels right directionally but we should change wording from "~45%" to a clearer range or context. Suggest: "reduced per-token inference cost by approximately 35–50% depending on workload and batching."
- Technical detail: in the third paragraph we should specify that the savings are post-quantization and include caching; current wording might imply savings that apply to out-of-the-box models.
- Attribution: can we swap the quote credit line to "— Sophie Li, Head of Marketing, TideWave Analytics" (you can provide exact attribution if you'd prefer).

I've looped in Ben from Marketing/CS for factual passback on the customer numbers and Marissa from Comms for publishing cadence and legal flags. Ben — can you review the two metrics calls and confirm the 35–50% range is safe? Marissa — any compliance/PII concerns in the draft?

If helpful, we can do a 20-minute sync tomorrow to walk the draft.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Sr. Customer Marketing Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sophie Li <sophie.li@tidewave.io>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-11T08:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft case study + quote — can you review

On Tue, Aug 10, 2026 at 10:23 AM Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> Thanks, Sophie — nice first pass. A few quick notes from product/marketing perspective:
> 
> - Quote accuracy: the number feels right directionally but we should change wording from "~45%" to a clearer range or context. Suggest: "reduced per-token inference cost by approximately 35–50% depending on workload and batching."

Quick factual passback from my side after checking the pilot telemetry: the 35–50% range is reasonable if we restrict to their 8–16k token average sessions and include the batching/caching configuration they used. If we generalize across all workloads the average drops to ~30%, so we should keep the phrasing tight to avoid misinterpretation.

I've attached a PDF with inline redlines (TideWave_redlines_from_CS.pdf) with a few specific suggestions: tighten the savings language, clarify the model family used (Redwood-FTL-7B quantized int8), and remove the paragraph that mentions exact latency numbers (we prefer ranges). Also flagged a line in the quote where TideWave calls Redwood "best-in-class" — marketing can keep it but legal might want a softer phrasing.

Acceptance checklist for publish:
- Final quote attribution (Sophie to confirm)
- Redlines accepted or countered (Sophie)
- Headshot + company logo (Sophie)
- Signed approval indicating permission to publish

If Sophie agrees to the redlines, we can push to finalize by 8/18 and schedule publish for 8/20.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Customer Success & Marketing Operations
Redwood Inference
Attachments: TideWave_redlines_from_CS.pdf (pdf, 95 KB)

From: Sophie Li <sophie.li@tidewave.io>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@tidewave.io>
Date: 2026-08-12T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft case study + quote — can you review

Thanks Ben/Hannah — appreciate the detailed pass. Alex and I reviewed the redlines and the changes look good. Specifics:

- Quote language: we'll accept the suggested phrasing: "reduced per-token inference cost by approximately 35–50% depending on workload and batching."
- Model family: we'll confirm "Redwood-FTL-7B (int8)" as the configuration used — Alex confirms that's accurate.
- Softening: we'll change "best-in-class" to "a reliable solution that materially lowered our operating cost."

I attached a quick one-line signed approval for publishing (signed_quote_approved.txt). We'll also send a hi-res headshot and our company logo by EOD tomorrow. No legal blocks from our side.

If you need a final sign-off from our CMO, I can cc her in the final message, but we're good to proceed.

Best,
Sophie Li
Head of Marketing, TideWave Analytics
Attachments: signed_quote_approved.txt (text, 1 KB)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sophie Li <sophie.li@tidewave.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-13T16:43:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft case study + quote — can you review

Excellent — thanks for the quick turnaround, Sophie. Final next steps from Redwood:

1) We'll incorporate Ben's redlines and replace the quote with the agreed phrasing.
2) Marissa will prepare the final publish copy and social assets; Marissa, target to have the final draft to TideWave by 8/17 for a last read.
3) Sophie — please send headshot + logo to this thread (or via the Drive link) by EOD 8/14 so we can lock the layout.
4) Once TideWave confirms the final draft, we'll go live with the case study on 2026-08-20 and push the social announcement the same day.

If anything changes on your side (CMO sign-off), loop us in but we won't wait unless you ask.

Thanks again — looking forward to publishing this together.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Sr. Customer Marketing Manager
Redwood Inference
